environmental.intro: All figures are estimates. CO₂ and water are derived from a published benchmark of LLM inference energy, weighted by token type and scaled per model; analogies use average reference values. Treat these as order-of-magnitude indicators, not precise measurements.
environmental.methodology.heading: Calculation & Estimates
environmental.methodology.cost: Cost (UBB) uses GitHub Copilot AI Credit rates (1 credit = $0.01) under Usage Based Billing.
environmental.methodology.co2Paper: CO₂: Jegham et al. estimate 5.671 Wh for one Claude 3.7 Sonnet request with 10,000 input and 1,500 output tokens; at 0.287 kg CO₂e/kWh (AWS) that is about 1.63 g CO₂e. Counting an input token as 1/20 of an output token, that request is 2,000 output-equivalent tokens, giving ~814 g (range 770–857 g) per 1M output-equivalent tokens, rounded up to 840 g.
environmental.methodology.co2Weights: Token weights (output = 1.0, uncached input = 0.05, cache write = 0.0625, cache read = 0.0005) are approximations adopted from neuland/tokendashboard-backend, not values from the paper. The paper does not model prompt caching, and the cache-read weight in particular is a rough guess. Tokens without a per-model breakdown are counted with the reference request's input/output mix.
environmental.methodology.modelScaling: Other models are scaled from the Claude Sonnet baseline by the ratio of their output-token price (for example Haiku ⅓×, Opus 1⅔×). Price stands in for model size here; it is not a measurement. Models without a known price use the Sonnet baseline.
environmental.methodology.water: Water uses the paper's formula: on-site cooling (energy ÷ PUE × 0.18 L/kWh) plus off-site electricity generation (energy × 5.11 L/kWh), with AWS's PUE of 1.14. That is about 30 mL for the reference request, or ~15 L per 1M output-equivalent tokens for Claude Sonnet, scaled per model like CO₂.
environmental.methodology.tree: Tree equivalent represents the fraction of a single mature tree's annual CO₂ absorption (~21 kg/year).
environmental.methodology.co2Analogies: CO₂ analogies: petrol car ≈ 120 g/km · intercity train ≈ 41 g/km · economy flight ≈ 180 g/km (ICAO avg.) · smartphone charge ≈ 8 g · LED bulb ≈ 3 g/hr (10 W, EU grid) · kettle boil ≈ 20 g.
environmental.methodology.waterAnalogies: Water analogies: shower ≈ 8 L/min · washing machine ≈ 50 L · standard bathtub ≈ 150 L · dishwasher ≈ 12 L · mug of tea ≈ 250 mL · daily drinking water ≈ 2 L/person.
environmental.methodology.caveat: All analogies are order-of-magnitude estimates. Actual values depend on your region's energy mix, hardware, model implementation, and caching behavior.
environmental.methodology.paperLink: Jegham et al., "How Hungry is AI?" (arXiv:2505.09598)

usage.claudeDesktopCoverage.tooltip:
Claude Desktop lists every session it knows about, but this extension can only measure sessions whose transcript is still on this machine. Two things remove a transcript from local disk:

• Claude Code deletes transcripts older than its retention window (the cleanupPeriodDays setting, 30 days by default). Raise it in ~/.claude/settings.json to keep more history measurable.
• Sessions that ran in the cloud never write a transcript to this machine at all.

These sessions are not missing from your account — they are just not measurable locally.

agentic.modes.title: How you work with agents
agentic.modes.subtitle: Last {0} days, {1} classified turns. Director sets intent and hands work off, performer changes things, assessor checks the result.
agentic.modes.delegation: {0} of sessions delegated work to another agent.
agentic.modes.lowAssessor: {0}% of your sessions hand work to agents, but only {1}% of turns check the result. Handing work off without checking it is how fast work turns into rework.
agentic.modes.how: Each turn's task category is mapped to a mode: Planning, Brainstorming and Delegation are director; Coding, Feature Dev, Refactoring, Debugging, Build/Deploy and Git Ops are performer; Testing is assessor. Exploration counts as director before the first change in a session and as assessor after it. Conversation is not counted. This is a heuristic.
agentic.matrix.title: Adoption × foundations
agentic.matrix.subtitle: Where each repository's agent use stands against its governance and shared-knowledge controls, from GitHub's Agentic Engineering System. Adoption is your own agent sessions in the last {0} days; foundations are the stage 1–3 controls below. Local to this machine — never uploaded or shared.
agentic.matrix.action.healthy-underused: Delegate small, well-bounded tasks to agents.
agentic.matrix.action.healthy-agent-nati: Expand to the next safe class of work.
agentic.matrix.action.underdeveloped: Strengthen the foundations before expanding agent use.
agentic.matrix.action.stretched: Agent use has outrun the controls: narrow scope and repair the missing controls.
agentic.matrix.chipTitle: Foundations {0} of {1} observed controls present, {2} not checked · {3} of {4} sessions used an agent
agentic.matrix.stretchedRepair: Controls missing in stretched repositories, lowest stage first:
agentic.matrix.unassessed.too-few-contro: too few controls could be checked
agentic.matrix.unassessed.no-remote: no GitHub remote to match sessions to
agentic.matrix.adoptionOnlyTitle: Agent use in repositories not open in this workspace (open one to assess its foundations):
agentic.matrix.how: Foundations: the share of stage 1–3 controls found present among those the scan could observe; controls it could not check are left out, not counted as missing. Strong is 70% or more; weak is 40% or less, or no tests running in CI, or no agent instruction file at all. Anything between leans to the nearer side (dashed). High agent use: at least 5 agent sessions in the window, making up at least 30% of the repository's sessions. The unit is always the repository; this is not a score of any person.
agentic.quality.title: Quality alongside adoption
agentic.quality.note: This month so far vs last month. Does not change your score, and is not part of any export.
agentic.quality.verdict.faster-and-stead: You are using agents more, and rework is flat or falling. That is the pattern to keep: faster without getting weaker.
agentic.quality.verdict.faster-but-weake: You are using agents more, but rework is rising with it. Speed that comes with more corrections usually means tasks are under-scoped or the agent lacks context.
agentic.quality.verdict.rework-rising: Agent use is steady, but rework is rising. Check the Corrections tab for the repositories driving it.
agentic.quality.verdict.steady: Agent use and rework are both steady compared with last month.
agentic.quality.verdict.insufficient-dat: Too early in the month to compare — check back after the first week.
Not enough sessions with per-turn detail in one of the two months to compare yet.
